prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet, single image, fully transparent background.

SUBJECT: the undead zombie basketball player in the attached reference image.
Match that character exactly: sickly grey-green skin, ragged mid-brown hair,
sunken eyes with small pale pupils, a lipless grin showing the teeth, dark
rotted patches on the arms and legs, a torn and ragged blue sleeveless
basketball jersey with a yellow number 13, torn blue shorts with white and
yellow trim, white high-top sneakers with blue and yellow flashes over white
socks. Identical colours, identical proportions, identical build and identical
height as the reference, in every frame.

LAYOUT: one horizontal row of 7 frames of equal width, evenly spaced. No
borders, no frame numbers, no labels, no background, no drop shadows.

CAMERA: locked off. Identical distance and eye level in every frame. The
character must be exactly the same height in every frame, and the same height
as in the reference image — do not zoom, crop, recompose or rescale between
frames. All frames share one ground line: whatever is touching the floor in a
given frame rests exactly on that line. He stays on the same spot on the floor
throughout.

VIEW: front view, facing the viewer.

He has just sunk a shot and celebrates so hard that he shakes himself to
pieces, then puts himself back together. Delighted throughout. Frames 2 to 7
are one continuous move.

FRAMES, left to right:
1. CALIBRATION POSE: standing straight upright, feet shoulder-width apart, arms
   hanging relaxed at his sides, facing the viewer, in the plain neutral
   standing pose from the reference image. This exact pose appears as the first
   frame of every sheet in this set and must be drawn identically every time.
2. Both arms thrown straight up overhead in triumph, jaw dropped wide in a
   groaning cheer, up on his toes.
3. Shaking himself apart at the top of the cheer — both arms detaching at the
   shoulders and flying upward, head lifting clear of the neck, the torso still
   upright.
4. A loose heap on the floor: legs folded, torso toppled across them, both arms
   and the head scattered around him on the ground line, the head face-up and
   still grinning.
5. Reassembling: the torso rising back onto the legs, one arm swinging back
   toward its shoulder, the head floating up toward the neck.
6. Nearly whole again: both arms reattached but crooked, the head settling onto
   the neck at a slight angle, wobbling upright.
7. Standing whole, both fists raised at chest height, head straight, a wide
   lipless grin — then easing down into a low athletic stance.

This is a one-shot, not a loop. Frame 2 must continue naturally from a low
athletic standing stance, and frame 7 must settle back into that same stance.

His own detached parts are the only extra elements and all of them stay within
his own frame.

STYLE: VGA-era 256-colour DOS-game pixel art, drawn pixel by pixel — NOT a
modern illustration with a pixel filter over it. The limits below are the look;
keep all of them: - At most THREE tones per material: a base, one darker
shadow, one lighter highlight. Hard edges between the tones. - NO gradients, NO
soft or airbrushed shading, NO glow, NO bloom, and NO anti-aliasing anywhere —
not on the outline, not between tones, not around the silhouette. - Where a
tone change needs softening, use visible ORDERED DITHER — a checkerboard of the
two tones. Dither, never blend. - Chunky square pixels on one consistent grid,
plainly visible at full size. - A bold dark outline around the silhouette and
around the major forms inside it. The background must be fully transparent
(alpha 0) with no haze, glow or soft fringe around the silhouette. Output a
wide landscape image.

The character is NOT holding a basketball in any frame — the ball is drawn
separately by the game.
